title: Wrong file ownership in rootless container export created with --userns=keep-id
body:
### Issue Description

When running `podman export ...` on a rootless container which has been created by `podman create --userns=keep-id ...` the file ownerships in the exported tarball are not as one would expect.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

The script below reproduces the bug, at the end it shows an expected and an actual file listing:

```bash
#!/bin/bash

podman build -t test - << EOF
FROM debian:13-slim
RUN useradd -m user
EOF

echo -e "\nls in container:\n"

podman run --rm test ls -lan /home/user

echo -e "\nregular export (expected):\n"

cid1=$(podman create test)
podman export "$cid1" | tar tv home

echo -e "\nexport with create --userns=keep-id (actual):\n"

cid2=$(podman create --userns=keep-id test)
podman export "$cid2" | tar tv home
```

Trunacted output:

```
ls in container:

total 20
drwx------ 2 1000 1000 4096 Sep 29 13:55 .
drwxr-xr-x 1    0    0 4096 Sep 29 13:55 ..
-rw-r--r-- 1 1000 1000  220 Jul 12 16:58 .bash_logout
-rw-r--r-- 1 1000 1000 3526 Jul 12 16:58 .bashrc
-rw-r--r-- 1 1000 1000  807 Jul 12 16:58 .profile

regular export (expected):

drwxr-xr-x 0/0               0 2026-09-29 13:55 home/
drwx------ 1000/1000         0 2026-09-29 13:55 home/user/
-rw-r--r-- 1000/1000       220 2026-07-12 16:58 home/user/.bash_logout
-rw-r--r-- 1000/1000      3526 2026-07-12 16:58 home/user/.bashrc
-rw-r--r-- 1000/1000       807 2026-07-12 16:58 home/user/.profile

export with create --userns=keep-id (actual):

drwxr-xr-x 1/1               0 2026-09-29 13:55 home/
drwx------ 0/0               0 2026-09-29 13:55 home/user/
-rw-r--r-- 0/0             220 2026-07-12 16:58 home/user/.bash_logout
-rw-r--r-- 0/0            3526 2026-07-12 16:58 home/user/.bashrc
-rw-r--r-- 0/0             807 2026-07-12 16:58 home/user/.profile
```

### Describe the results you received

Files owned by UID 1000 inside the container get exported to the tarball as owned by UID 0.

### Describe the results you expected

Files owned by UID 1000 inside the container get exported to the tarball as owned by UID 1000.

comments.body:
This isn't specific to running podman inside a container. Same result on an ordinary host: Raspberry Pi OS (Debian 13, arm64, kernel 6.18), Debian's `podman 5.4.2`, rootless as UID 1000 with the stock `100000:65536` subuid range. Image = `debian:13-slim` + `useradd -m user`. The keep-id container's mapping is `["0:1:1000","1000:0:1","1001:1001:64536"]`; the plain one has `IDMappings null`.

It's the whole tree, not just `home/`. Owner counts over the full archive:

```
plain export:   3257 0/0    7 0/42    5 1000/1000    3 0/43    1 0/8
keep-id export: 3257 1/1    7 1/43    5 0/0          3 1/44    1 1/9
```

So the setuid binaries (`su`, `passwd`, `mount`, ... 8 of them) come out `-rwsr-xr-x 1/1`. After `podman import`, `/etc/passwd` is `1:1`, `/usr/bin/su` is setuid UID 1, and `podman run --user user e2img touch /home/user/x` fails with `Permission denied` (the original image works). Both exports exit 0.

`podman cp ctr:/ - | tar tv` on the same keep-id container shifts the same way (user's files `root/root`, root's `daemon/daemon`), so it isn't a workaround.

What does work: `podman commit` the keep-id container, `podman create` a plain container from that image, export that. Owners come out right, including files written at runtime (`home/user/made-at-runtime.txt 1000/1000`, `root/made-by-root.txt 0/0`, `usr/bin/su 0/0`).

Looks like the cause is in `Container.export()` (`libpod/container_internal.go`): `chrootarchive.Tar(mountPoint, nil, mountPoint)` passes no `TarOptions`, so no `UIDMaps`/`GIDMaps`, and the storage, which for keep-id is on disk under the intermediate IDs (`podman unshare` + `podman mount` shows the user's file as `0 0` and root's as `1 1`), is archived as-is. That line is identical at v5.4.2, v5.8.7 and main.

Write-up: https://homelabpostmortem.com/2026/09/30/podman-export-of-a-keep-id-container-shifts-every-owner/
